result.summary: Executed WF-02 Step 4 for REQ-036, following docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-036.md (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved) exactly. Wrote both new test files verbatim from the spec's own source blocks -- apps/bot/src/scheduler/urgencyJobs.db.test.ts (tg_id 1_030_000_000+, AC1 + AC7 urgency-side) and apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts (tg_id 1_031_000_000+, AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6-inline/AC7-autodecline-side/AC8) -- with zero edits beyond transcription. `npm run lint -w apps/bot` (eslint .) ran clean, zero errors/warnings. `npm run build -w apps/bot` (tsc -p tsconfig.json) ran clean, zero type errors. Full-suite `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` was run from the repo root (never a subdirectory root, per the mandate) TWICE: attempt 1 was already clean -- 41/41 test files, 367/367 individual tests, 45.91s; attempt 2, run purely for extra confidence given ISS-0031's documented shared-Postgres cross-process contention pattern, reproduced the identical clean result -- 41/41 files, 367/367 tests, 41.46s. No retry was actually needed to reach a conclusive signal (attempt 1 alone was already conclusive and clean); a second run was made anyway as a consistency check, and it matched. A third, isolated run of just the two new REQ-036 files (`npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/scheduler/urgencyJobs.db.test.ts apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts`) also passed cleanly: 2/2 files, 9/9 tests (urgencyJobs.db.test.ts: 2 tests for AC1 and AC7-urgency-side; autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts: 7 tests for AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5 x2, AC7-autodecline-side, AC8). REQ-036's own two new test files were therefore consistently clean across all 3 executions this session (both full-suite runs plus the isolated run) -- no flakiness, no ISS-0031 contention symptom (no FK-violation errors, no varying failing-file set) observed at any point. AC8's process half was verified by directly reading handoffs/WF02-REQ-036/step-02-backend-dev.json's result.issues[0], per the spec's own instruction that this AC is confirmed by reading the record, not by test code -- confirmed present verbatim as the spec restates it. No spec/implementation mismatch was encountered anywhere; every case ran exactly as written against the real scheduler code with no test-code alteration to force a pass.
